author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Attleboro leaders and residents dedicated a new Global War on Terrorism Monument at Capron Park on Friday, placing a permanent marker for local military service in the city’s central public space. The memorial recognizes Attleboro service members who served in the conflicts and operations that followed the September 11, 2001, attacks.

The ceremony was held on the attacks’ 25th anniversary. Speakers emphasized that the human cost of the wars extended beyond combat deaths to veterans and families who continued to carry losses after deployments ended. The monument was organized by Attleboro’s Global War on Terrorism Committee, bringing the project from a community effort to a completed civic memorial.

Funding came from the state and from donations by residents and small businesses, according to NBC 10. That mix of public and local support made the dedication both a veterans observance and a community project. With the monument now installed in Capron Park, Attleboro has added a specific place for future ceremonies and private reflection on more than two decades of service connected to the post-September 11 era.
dek: The Capron Park memorial honors local service members who took part in the Global War on Terrorism and those whose losses continued after deployment.
headline: Attleboro dedicates monument to post-September 11 service
